objective.text: Distinguish owner-checked release from forceRelease when another process holds the lock.

difficulty.rationale: Identify the safety difference between normal release and an administrative force release.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: Process A holds an unexpired lock. Process B creates a lock object with the same name but a different owner token. How do B’s release() and forceRelease() differ?

options.text: release respects A’s ownership; forceRelease can remove A’s lock.
options.rationale: The ordinary operation checks the owner, while forceRelease intentionally bypasses that check.

options.text: Both operations automatically transfer A’s ownership to B.
options.rationale: Neither release operation is a lock-ownership transfer API.
options.misconception: Neither release operation is a lock-ownership transfer API.

options.text: Both operations fail unless B supplies A’s owner token.
options.rationale: That describes ordinary release, but not the force-release escape hatch.
options.misconception: That describes ordinary release, but not the force-release escape hatch.

options.text: release removes A’s lock, while forceRelease only extends its expiration.
options.rationale: This reverses ownership protection and misstates forceRelease as a renewal operation.
options.misconception: This reverses ownership protection and misstates forceRelease as a renewal operation.
